name: @southleft/sl-web-components
description: The Southleft brand design system — opinionated section components built on Altitude

..//: The `types` and `default` targets sit in DIFFERENT subtrees and that is not a typo. Vite writes the JS to `dist/components/…` (vite.config.mjs entry map). `tsc` writes the declarations one level deeper, under `dist/sl-web-components/components/…`, because this package's components import Altitude through RELATIVE paths (`../../../al-web-components/components/ALElement`), which pulls those sources into the tsc program and makes the inferred rootDir `libs/`, not `libs/sl-web-components`. Both halves were pointed at the vite layout, where no .d.ts has ever existed — the same class of break as the note on al-web-components' root export, and it was invisible while this package was `"private": true`. The emitted tree is internally consistent (`dist/sl-web-components/**` re-imports `dist/al-web-components/**` at exactly those relative depths), so it is the map that was wrong, not the emit. If those relative imports are ever replaced by the `@southleft/al-web-components` specifier, rootDir collapses to this package and these two paths must lose the `sl-web-components/` segment.

scripts.//build: NOT yet wired into the root `build:all` — the only consumer today is the Southleft Storybook, which compiles these sources directly through its own Vite. Wire it in when apps/southleft imports the package (spec 2026-08-22-southleft-brand-design-system-as-a-linked-layer-on-altitude, T11).
scripts.build: del-cli dist && vite build -c vite.config.mjs && tsc

//sideEffects: Source paths as well as dist, for the same reason as @southleft/al-web-components — see the note there. Every component module here ends in a `customElements.define` guarded by `alAutoRegistry`; if the bundler thinks the module is side-effect-free it drops the whole import and the element silently never upgrades in a production Storybook build.
